guide: Edit short videos from your phone by messaging an AI agent that runs an editing assistant on your own computer; you need a Telegram bot, an always-on computer with Claude Code and ffmpeg, a Google Drive folder and CapCut.
1. Create a Telegram bot with BotFather and connect it to an open-source agent framework (or a small script) running on the computer at home.
1. Have the agent send each draft video to you on Telegram as a preview, labelled with its version number.
1. Reply to the preview in plain text with the changes you want, such as "cut the pause after the hook" or "make the captions bigger".
1. Let the agent pass your message to Claude Code on that computer, which edits the video with ffmpeg and saves a new version.
1. Have the agent send the finished cut back to you on Telegram and copy it into a Google Drive folder.
1. Open that file in CapCut on your phone, clean up the voice yourself, listen to the audio, then post.
Watch out: let the agent do the cutting only; check the audio by ear in CapCut before you post.

```
You are helping me build a phone-controlled video editing workflow. I have a Telegram account, a computer that stays switched on at home with <operating system>, Claude Code installed, ffmpeg installed, a Google Drive folder called <folder name>, and CapCut on my phone.
Build a small agent that does the following:
1. Watches a folder on my computer for draft videos named <draft file pattern>.
2. Sends each draft to me on Telegram through a bot, with a version number in the message.
3. Treats my next text reply as edit instructions, starts Claude Code on the computer with those instructions and the latest video, and has it make the edit with ffmpeg and save it as the next version.
4. Sends the finished version back on Telegram and copies it into my Google Drive folder.
Constraints: only respond to my Telegram user, keep the bot token in an environment variable, never overwrite earlier versions, and do not touch audio unless I ask. Return the full code, setup steps for the Telegram bot and Google Drive access, and one example conversation.
```
